body.x: RNware (President Young-Gyu Kim, www.anysync.co.kr) introduced the wireless transmitters "Anysync N:1 Type" and "Anysync 1:1 Type" at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

Anysync N:1 Type allows wireless-transmission of the images and sound on smart pads, PC, and camcorders for remote display, perfect for a variety of purposes such as class lectures, conference meetings, presentations, and entertainment.

High-quality images and sound can be wirelessly transmitted in real-time and without AP. Without any pauses or delays, the exact quality and content on the screen are mirrored identically. Furthermore, the numerous compatibility modes are not limited to a particular product, thus delivering the world’s first N:1 mirroring without the hassles of S/W or server program installation.

Anysync 1:1 Type also enables wireless-transmission of various devices’ images and sounds for remote display. All contents are transmitted for real-time mirroring, and the device support s1:1 connection. As the device wirelessly mirrors a PC or a tablet screen onto a larger screen, it is ideal for a meeting or a lesson in a conference room or a classroom without PC connection or paper distribution.

The company spokesperson stated, "Because not only companies but also individual clients utilize this product, we hope to attract large interest from the North American distributers and buyers through this tradeshow."

RNware is a wireless image-transmission embedded venture corporation, with a strong foundation in touch sensor and image transmission. The company is targeting the smart education market as well as the smart conference market and possesses three trademark applications and six patents in the related field.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
